data.name: Big Bad Pharma
data.detailed_description:
12,792 items. One unbelievable mess. You.

Clock in. Stock the shelves. Climb the ladder of an industry that maybe shouldn't exist.

Big Bad Pharma is a cosy first-person pharmacy-stocking sim with a wicked streak. On the surface it's everything you want from a tidy little restocking game: neat shelves, a quiet shop to run, and that deeply pleasing click of the last box sliding into place. Underneath, it's a cheeky satire of corporate healthcare, and the further up the ladder you climb, the more you might want to ask yourself whether it was worth it.

Every shift starts the same way: shelves stripped bare, product everywhere, and you.

Every single one of the 12,792 items on that floor has a home. A specific shelf, in a specific bay, in a specific aisle, and the shop isn't finished until every last one of them is in it. Pick things up, carry an armful, and slot them into place. Categories run from digestive relief to migraine remedies to a genuinely suspicious quantity of allergy medication, all of it wearing a label that's almost a brand you'd recognise. Legally speaking.

Forgotten where the antihistamines live? There's a catalogue book in your pocket. Whether you're a methodical shelf-perfectionist working one bay at a time or a chaotic box-flinger lobbing paracetamol across the room, the shop is yours to run.

Every shift starts the same way — empty shelves, a full stockroom, and you. Sort products into the right aisles, from digestive relief to migraine remedies to a suspicious number of allergy medications. Keep things tidy, keep things moving, and try not to lose an item along the way. Whether you're a methodical shelf-perfectionist or a chaotic box-flinger, the shop is yours to run.

Nobody climbs the corporate ladder on foot forever.

Behind the staff door there's a beige desktop PC running an operating system that time forgot. That's the Rx Upgrade Hub, and it's where your wages go. Carry more in one trip. Move faster between aisles. Jump higher, throw further, and unlock the four tools that turn a long shift into a short one:

  • Locate: light up every stray item of a category, wherever it's hiding

  • Auto Shelve: send what's in your hands straight to where it belongs

  • Magnet: pull nearby product to you without bending down once

  • Sweep: gather up a whole patch of floor in a single pass

Max everything out and you become a truly well-rounded (and slightly terrifying) employee of the month.

There's more to this pharmacy than restocking. Twenty-one achievements trace your journey from bleary-eyed newcomer to something a little more... corporate. There are things written on mirrors. There's a radio out back with four decades of music on it. There's a toilet, and yes, it flushes.

Clock out at the end of a shift and the numbers come up: items shelved, sections completed, time on the floor, and a running record of every shift you've ever worked. Then the shop refills, the day ticks over, and it all starts again, which is either deeply comforting or the entire joke, depending on how you're feeling.

Big Bad Pharma is warm, funny, satisfying to play, and just self-aware enough to make you smirk. It's a game about small satisfactions and big questions, made by one person with a sharp sense of humour and far too much time spent thinking about shelf geometry.

Plays on mouse and keyboard or controller, in five-minute bursts or three-hour ones.

Come for the shelves. Stay for the slow moral decline.

AI Content Disclaimer (NO AI): This game was created with love and passion for learning to create a game after games being the one consistent in my life. All 3D assets are my own (hence why I kept it very basic). All textures and decals in game are made by me (you may see where I've struggled in places). I have recently removed AI generated achievement images and replaced them with my own designs, the same applies to all Steam Graphics, Logos and background images. Officially NO AI.

data.short_description: A cosy first-person pharmacy sim with a wicked streak. 12,792 items. One unbelievable mess. Stock the shelves, buy the upgrades, and climb a corporate ladder that probably shouldn't exist. Then try not to think too hard about what's at the top.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit (Build 19041 or later)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 / AMD Ryzen 5 2600
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 / AMD Radeon RX 560 (2GB VRAM)
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
  • Sound Card: DirectX 9.0c compatible
  • Additional Notes: Requires 64-bit processor and operating system
